# ssp_upgrade (Resource)

Triggers and tracks an in-place SSP cluster upgrade.

The SSP upgrade workflow has no user-selectable target version and no request
body: `POST /ssp/upgrade` is driven entirely by the `action` query parameter
(`PRECHECKS_ONLY`, `START`, `CONTINUE`, `RETRY`), and `target_version` /
`current_version` are read-only values reported by `GET /ssp/upgrade/status`
once an upgrade version has been staged in the depot.

On create, the resource deploys the `UPGRADE_COORDINATOR` feature, then:

- if the last upgrade attempt is `FAILED`, issues `action=RETRY`;
- else if `run_prechecks` is `true` (default), issues `action=PRECHECKS_ONLY`
    first and only proceeds to `action=CONTINUE` if pre-checks succeed;
- else issues `action=START` directly.

On destroy, the `UPGRADE_COORDINATOR` feature is undeployed. There is only one
upgrade workflow per SSP cluster, so this resource is a singleton.

Corresponds to `POST /ssp/upgrade` and `GET /ssp/upgrade/status`.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `run_prechecks` (Boolean) Whether to run validation pre-checks before starting the upgrade. Ignored if a previous upgrade attempt failed (in which case the failed attempt is retried via `action=RETRY`).

### Read-Only

- `current_step` (String) Display name of the upgrade step currently executing (or the last step executed).
- `current_version` (String) SSP version the cluster was running immediately before the upgrade, as reported by the API.
- `id` (String) Fixed identifier (`upgrade`); the SSP API exposes a single cluster-wide upgrade workflow.
- `progress` (Number) Percentage of upgrade steps that have completed successfully (0–100).
- `status` (String) Overall status of the upgrade operation (`NOT_STARTED`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `SUCCESS`, `FAILED`).
- `target_version` (String) SSP version the cluster is being upgraded to, as reported by the API. Not user-settable — `POST /ssp/upgrade` has no version parameter.
